about:
Badlands Steel operates in Williston, North Dakota. The company was born out of a growing need for steel fabrication in the Williston area, though no founding year or founders are disclosed, and ownership structure is not specified.

The shop provides steel fabrication, steel products, and steel services using what it describes as state-of-the-art equipment to handle all aspects of steel fabrication. It works with carbon steel, aluminum, and stainless steel, offering custom products for a range of applications. No facility size, headcount, or production volumes are published.

The company serves customers in the oil field, natural gas, industrial, construction, and agriculture sectors. These industries are listed directly on its homepage as primary markets, reflecting the regional economy around the Bakken formation.

Badlands Steel says it is devoted to providing high-quality products and was started to fill a local gap in steel fabrication capability. It emphasizes its ability to meet all steel fabrication needs under one roof, from raw material to finished component.

name: Baker Medical, Inc.
old_description: is a locally-owned and operated medical supply store based in Conway, Arkansas. For more than 10 years, we've been helping individuals and healthcare professionals from all over the state of Arkansas care for themselves and their patients by offering medical supplies and equipment.
about:
Baker Medical, Inc. operates as a locally owned medical supply retailer in Conway, Arkansas, with a second location in Clinton. The company has served the state for nearly two decades, though a precise founding year is not published. It began as a neighborhood store focused on providing medical equipment and supplies directly to patients and healthcare providers across Arkansas.

The business stocks and ships a range of home healthcare products, including CPAP and BiPAP systems, catheters, incontinence supplies, diabetic and insulin pump accessories, and oral supplements. A respiratory therapist on staff performs daily CPAP setups, and the company runs a resupply program that mails fresh consumables to patients’ doors. Orders over $20 ship free via USPS, with processing within one business day and delivery in one to three days anywhere in Arkansas. The two storefronts serve as both retail counters and service centers.

Customers include individual patients managing chronic conditions at home as well as clinics and home health agencies that refer patients for equipment and ongoing supply management. The company bills most insurance plans with a valid prescription, positioning itself as an intermediary between prescribers, payers, and end users.

Baker Medical emphasizes its clinical support—particularly the respiratory therapist-led CPAP setups—and its Arkansas-focused logistics as key differentiators. The ownership describes the mission as improving patients’ quality of life through accessible equipment and responsive service.

about:
Balance Clothing Company is a custom design and print shop based in Charleston, West Virginia. Founded in 2007 by David Collins, the business began as a search for harmony between creative process, printing, and design. The company has grown steadily since its start.

The firm operates an in-house screen printing and vinyl workshop, offering a range of services including screen printing, logo design, vehicle wraps (car, boat, building, wall), large-format prints such as posters, banners, and signage (3-D lettering, Lexan and metal signs, booth backdrops, stickers, tents, feather flags, corrugated plastic signs), and collateral like business cards, brochures, and postcards. Clients are paired with an artist to tailor each project for print.

Balance serves clients across multiple states, with noted accounts in Chicago, Columbus, Cincinnati, and Hawaii. Its work spans apparel decoration, vehicle and marine graphics, architectural signage, trade-show displays, and promotional products for businesses and organizations.

Collins started the company to bridge the gap between concept and production, emphasizing a personal client experience. The team stresses relationship-building over transactional jobs and continuously sources new apparel styles and vinyl materials to expand options.

name: Bald Ridge Enterprises, LLC
old_description: Bald Ridge Enterprises is the trusted name for sheet metal in Wyoming and Montana, delivering precision craftsmanship in architectural sheet metal and metal construction. From custom roofing and siding to premanufactured metal buildings, our work is built to perform and designed to last.
about:
Bald Ridge Enterprises operates from Cody, Wyoming, where it was founded nearly four decades ago as a small local shop built on family values. The company is registered as a Women-Owned Small Business with the U.S. federal government and has grown into a regional contractor serving Wyoming and Montana.

The company provides complete metal construction services, specializing in architectural sheet metal fabrication and installation. Its in-house shop produces pre-manufactured steel buildings, metal roofing systems, siding, soffits, fascia, gutters, downspouts, and specialty items such as snow bars, chimney caps, and custom planter boxes. A carpentry division adds wood detailing to projects. All components are designed, fabricated, and installed by the company's own crews, giving it control over quality from start to finish.

Bald Ridge serves commercial, agricultural, residential, institutional, and government customers across the two-state area. Projects range from personal shops and farm structures to large-scale institutional and government facilities. The company's online design tool allows clients to configure building layouts and request quotes remotely.

The firm differentiates itself by building to the Architectural Sheet Metal Manual, the industry's highest standard, and by engineering its systems for the extreme weather of Wyoming and Montana. It backs its work with a standard one-year warranty plus extended manufacturer guarantees, and emphasizes a family-focused culture that has retained a certified, insured team for nearly 40 years.

about:
Ballard Sheet Metal Works Inc. has operated from Seattle, Washington, since 1907. The family-owned and operated business began over a century ago on Ballard Avenue Northwest, serving the Greater Puget Sound area with custom metal fabrication.

The shop provides a wide range of fabrication services, including flashing, backsplashes, corner guards, sill pans, thresholds, countertops with integrated sinks, custom sinks, hoods, fireplace surrounds, barbecues, planter boxes, railings, stairs, awnings, and chimney caps. It also handles marine projects such as fire dampers, custom HVAC components, welding, and tanks. Shearing capacity runs from 24‑gauge material up to 3/8‑inch steel sheet at 10‑foot lengths, and the company works with galvanized steel, hot‑ and cold‑rolled steel, aluminum, prepainted steel, stainless steel, copper, zinc, Cor‑Ten, brass, and diamond plate. Certified welders perform both shop and field welding, and field measurement and installation are available.

Customers include local contractors, architects, and residential homeowners across the Puget Sound region. The company’s marine work serves the maritime industry, while its HVAC and architectural metalwork support commercial and residential construction. Reviews highlight projects for homeowners needing custom countertops, fireplace surrounds, and boat repairs.

The firm emphasizes its team’s experience and the ability to handle projects of any size, from small residential jobs to large commercial contracts. Its long history and in‑house fabrication and installation capabilities are cited as key differentiators.

about:
Barbett Industries Inc. operates from Reading, Pennsylvania, where it manufactures narrow fabrics. The company is led by President Frank J. Loos and his son, General Manager Joseph Loos, indicating a family-run operation.

The firm produces a broad line of custom and commodity narrow fabrics, including braids, cords, and trims such as twist cord, draw cord, lamp shade trim, Chinese braid, bolo cord, industrial braid, metallic braid, jacquard braids, and various fringes. Finishing processes encompass custom dyeing, acetate tipping, hot and cold cutting, metal barbing, cord and tassel assembly, textile crimping, and waxing. The manufacturing shop is located in the United States, though facility size and headcount are not disclosed.

Barbett serves apparel manufacturers, producers of braided vinyl and leather goods, fishing lure makers, flag component suppliers, home furnishings companies, industrial clients, and military uniform trim contractors. The company also replicates customer samples and provides production cost estimates, and accepts customer-supplied goods for finishing work.

Barbett emphasizes its status as an independent domestic textile manufacturer that competes on quality and price, with the ability to replicate customer samples and advise on production costs, and to process customer-owned materials through its finishing operations.

name: Barku Plastics
old_description: Barku has been producing high-quality plastic parts for 40 years. Precision parts using injection molding technology as well as profiles and pipes using extrusion processes are manufactured quickly and reliably.
about:
Barku Plastics operates from Cleveland, Tennessee. The company traces its roots to 1977 when Egon Schumacher founded it as a subsidiary of LUBING Maschinenfabrik GmbH in Germany. Barku Plastics L.L.C. was established in Cleveland in September 2003 as a subsidiary of Barku Kunststofftechnik GmbH, maintaining German ownership.

The company specializes in custom plastic injection molding and profile extrusion. It runs more than 50 injection molding machines ranging from 32 to 1,100 tons, and over 10 extrusion lines capable of diameters up to 6 inches and profile widths up to 39 3/8 inches. Processes include two-component and insert molding, as well as co-extrusion for multi-material products. The facility operates three shifts and processes more than 14,000 tons of raw material annually. Materials processed include PP, PE, PS, PVC, POM, ABS, PU, and PA. Barku also provides assembly services, engineering support, mold development, and packaging of multi-part assemblies.

Barku serves customers worldwide across various industries, though specific sectors are not named in the input. The company works with clients needing precision injection-molded parts and extruded profiles and pipes, offering development, design, series production, and further processing.

Barku emphasizes flexibility, know-how, and a commitment to high quality standards, reflected in its ISO 9001:2015 certification with TUV Rheinland. The company highlights its partnerships with mold builders on three continents and continuous optimization of production processes through machine park renewal and employee training.

name: Barn XO
old_description: It’s our privilege to reclaim rare Midwestern woods originally harvested during Chicago’s industrial rise in the late 1800s and early 1900s. Their rich history lives on through every knot, grain, and imperfection.
about:
Barn XO operates from Mundelein, Illinois, where the family-owned business reclaims rare Midwestern woods originally harvested during Chicago's industrial rise in the late 1800s and early 1900s. The company was founded on the premise of preserving the history embedded in each knot, grain, and imperfection of this reclaimed lumber.

The workshop produces custom handcrafted furniture including conference tables, bar and dining tables, chairs and bar stools, desks, console tables, and coffee tables. Each piece is built to order through a process that begins with a design consultation, continues with material and finish selection at the company's showroom, and ends with nationwide delivery.

Barn XO serves both residential and commercial clients. Homeowners order dining tables, benches, and coffee tables for private residences, while businesses specify conference tables for offices and bar-height tables for hospitality venues. The company's portfolio includes pieces for corporate boardrooms, restaurants, and home offices.

The brand differentiates itself by emphasizing sustainable design that honors the origins of its materials. Barn XO states that its furniture carries the history of Chicago's industrial past, and it markets its products as made in the USA with free design consultations and a showroom experience in Mundelein.

name: Barrett Petfood
old_description: Barrett Petfood was founded on a simple promise: If we wouldn’t feed it to our own pets, you won’t find it in our products. We help pets and pet food companies thrive by delivering a premium manufacturing and brand services experience that takes pet food from idea to bowl with integrity.
about:
Barrett Petfood is headquartered in Brainerd, Minnesota. The company was founded in 2006 when agricultural entrepreneur Mike Barrett purchased a piece of equipment intended for agricultural manufacturing, only to discover it was suited for food production. Mike and his children, Tom and Sarah Barrett, pivoted the business into pet food, with Mike later transitioning ownership to his children while continuing to supply ingredients from his farm. The company remains family-owned.

Barrett operates two facilities in central Minnesota: the original Brainerd plant and a second site opened in 2020 in Little Falls that added 160,000 square feet and two production lines. The company produces hundreds of formulas across super‑premium kibble, kibble‑plus, and freeze‑dried formats, using extrusion, milling, and automated packaging lines. Its capabilities span diet formulation, ingredient sourcing, processing, packaging, and distribution.

Barrett serves pet food brands ranging from emerging labels to market leaders, manufacturing diets for dogs, cats, reptiles, birds, livestock, and zoo animals. Customers rely on the company as a full‑service co‑manufacturer that handles everything from formulation to shipping.

The business was built on a simple promise: “If we wouldn’t feed it to our own pets, you won’t find it in our products.” The Barretts emphasize a relationship‑based philosophy, a “Don’t Say No” innovation mindset, and rigorous, laboratory‑like food‑safety standards as their differentiators.
